tasks.short: Supervise, train and schedule childcare staff

steps.what: Check staffing needs, availability, qualifications and required coverage before scheduling
Prepare, verify and issue work schedules and assignments to childcare staff
Supervise staff in practice, give feedback and respond to care or personnel issues
Train staff in care routines and check their practical understanding

tasks.design: Use native roster copying and assignment fields in {HCM} or {CALENDAR} to prepare the schedule from a checked staffing brief. The worker verifies coverage and issues the exact roster, while supervision, feedback and practical training remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring roster entry sits beside decisions about suitable coverage and staff support.
tasks.enabler_now: Native roster reuse can reduce repeated entry without scoring staff or deciding suitability automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected absence, changing child attendance and whether a person is ready for an assignment.
tasks.human_edge: Judge practical readiness, coach staff and resolve sensitive personnel concerns.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated roster entry; care coverage and people decisions stay within existing delegated authority.

reach.task: Resolve a coverage gap that exceeds the worker's scheduling authority
reach.learn: Qualification requirements, escalation and staffing constraints

evidence.claim: Native roster reuse and calendar assignment fields can reduce repeated schedule entry, while coverage suitability and staff development remain human decisions.

assumptions: Boundary includes personnel functions actually delegated to the childcare worker, not changing employment terms, hiring or making final disciplinary decisions. Staff members' own care and training attendance time is outside the focal denominator.

In s1 the worker obtains and captures staff ids, available times, proposed shifts, room or group, required coverage and qualification references. All 15 hours remain for availability discussion, checking and capture. Attendance coordinator and personnel administrator already maintain planned child attendance and qualification source records outside this task; that unchanged capture earns no saving.

s2 retains 15 hours for choosing assignments, checking breaks and coverage, resolving conflicts and confirming the completed roster. No machine infers qualification or suitability from a free-text personnel record.
Missing availability, unclear coverage rules or uncertain qualifications prevent reuse and require manual resolution. No automatic roster release or worker ranking is introduced.
Test native roster copying before custom code. Extra staff-input capture, if required, must be added rather than transferred for free; this design uses existing discussions in s1.
Approval binds the exact roster and assignments before issue; changes require review again. Supervision and practical training retain all 60 hours, and rule or mapping maintenance is costed below.
research_questions: Can native roster reuse shorten entry while preserving coverage checks and staff consultation?

already_counted.description: Verify staffing inputs, confirm schedules, supervise and train staff

incremental.description: Maintain roster patterns and check changed qualification or coverage mappings

approvals.approved_version: Completed roster revision with named staff, times, rooms and assignments; any edit voids confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=15+15+35+25=90; gross 10 less upkeep 1 gives net 9. E1 scenario reduces roster preparation by 40% on recurring shifts only; absence changes or existing roster reuse may leave no additional gain. Supervision and training time never falls.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The worker can prepare recurring rosters with less re-entry while preserving coverage judgement, supervision and staff training.
reach: Escalate difficult coverage gaps to the childcare supervisor
role.ambitious_version: A worker who spends less time reproducing schedules and retains the attention needed to support staff and safe care.
